examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
An implication p→q excludes only p=true,q=false. Contraposition preserves this forbidden assignment; the converse need not. Equivalence means agreement on every assignment, while satisfiability needs only one model. Refute entailment using a model of all premises with a false conclusion. CNF is an AND of clauses; DNF is an OR of conjunctions. De Morgan's laws exchange these operations under negation.

**Key relationship:** p → q ≡ ¬p ∨ q; ¬(p ∧ q) ≡ ¬p ∨ ¬q

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. Remove implications.
2. Push negations inward.
3. Seek a counterassignment before claiming entailment.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Convert implications before counting valuations: p→q is ¬p∨q. For validity, seek a valuation satisfying every premise and falsifying the conclusion; finding one disproves validity. For a tautology, prove that no falsifying row exists. A converse and an inverse have the same truth table as each other, but neither is generally equivalent to the original implication.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
How many valuations of p,q,r satisfy (p→q) AND (q→r)?

**Answer: 4.** If q=0, p must be 0 and r is free: 2 valuations. If q=1, r must be 1 and p is free: 2 more. Total 4. Equivalently these are the nondecreasing three-bit sequences 000,001,011,111.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
An implication with a false premise is true. Do not discard that row when counting models.

The converse q → p is not equivalent to p → q; the contrapositive ¬q → ¬p is.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

Which equals ¬(p→q)?

- **A.** ¬p∧q
- **B.** p∨¬q
- **C.** ¬p∨q
- **D.** p∧¬q

**Answer: D.** Replace implication with ¬p∨q, then negate using De Morgan: p∧¬q.

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

Select all tautologies.

- **A.** p∨¬p
- **B.** p→(p∧q)
- **C.** p→q
- **D.** (p→q)↔(¬q→¬p)

**Answer: A, D.** Excluded middle and contraposition are tautologies. Both remaining implications fail at p=true,q=false.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

How many assignments to p,q,r satisfy (p→q)∧(q→r)?



**Answer: 4.** The bits cannot fall from 1 to 0. The models are 000,001,011,111: four.

examGuide.title: Work through the supplied PYQs
examGuide.body:
#### GATE 2024 CS2 · Q12 · MCQ

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/propositional-logic?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Propositional logic. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. ‘When a student scores more than 50%’ establishes condition q. Under that condition, a fail grade cannot be given, which is ¬p.
2. The implication is therefore q→¬p. It does not assert that every non-failing student scored more than 50%.
3. Choose **A**; reversing an implication changes its meaning.
